# Refund when stock runs out after charging

> If the product sells out after Stripe has already charged the card, the service refunds the charge, marks the payment `REFUNDED`, and tells the caller the stock ran out.

_Part of [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md)_

This lives in `PaymentService.executePayment`. The service charges Stripe first, outside any database transaction. Then it opens the finalize transaction and runs the [Optimistic stock deduction](optimistic-stock-deduction.md) update. If that update changes zero rows, someone else bought the last items while we were charging. The service does not touch the `Payment` row. It leaves it `PENDING` and returns a result with `needsRefund: true` and the Stripe payment intent id. Back in `executePayment`, the code sees the `needsRefund` flag after the finalize transaction has ended. It calls `refundPaymentIntent` on [`StripeService`](../platform-stripe/stripe.md) inside a span called `Refund: Insufficient Stock`. It passes the same idempotency key as the charge, so a retry will not refund twice. Only after the refund succeeds does it open a second transaction. In that second transaction it sets the payment from `PENDING` to `REFUNDED`. It then writes an outbox message with a [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md). The caller gets the refunded payment plus that error. This is a small saga: charge, then undo with a refund, with no two-phase commit. See [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md) for the whole flow.

**Look at:** [`PaymentService.executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L65)

## Pieces

- Marker that says the charge must be refunded: The finalize transaction returns `needsRefund: true` with `stripePaymentIntentId` when the stock update affects zero rows, instead of changing the payment.
- Stripe refund done outside the database transaction: `refundPaymentIntent` is called after the finalize transaction ends, using the original idempotency key, so no database connection is held during the network call.
- Follow-up transaction that marks REFUNDED and notifies the caller: A second transaction updates the payment from `PENDING` to `REFUNDED` and writes an outbox message carrying [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md).

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| external | `Stripe payment intent refund` | `refundPaymentIntent` refunds the charge, using the payment intent id and the request's idempotency key. |
| database | `Payment` | Status goes from `PENDING` to `REFUNDED` in the follow-up transaction, only where the status is still `PENDING`. |
| database | `Product` | The `UPDATE` with `quantity >= :quantity` matching no row is what triggers the refund. |
| queue | `Outbox (via ``OutboxService.notify``)` | Stores the insufficient-stock error and the refunded payment for the caller, in the same transaction as the status change. |

## Also relies on

- [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md): This is the last step of the charging flow, after Stripe has charged the card.
- [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md): Uses the `Payment` model and `PaymentDtoService.update` to set `REFUNDED`.

## Watch out

- The payment stays `PENDING` while the refund happens. If the service dies between the refund and the status update, a retry sees `PENDING` again.
- The refund runs outside the transaction on purpose. A rolled-back transaction cannot undo a Stripe refund.
- The `REFUNDED` update only matches `PENDING` payments. A payment already in `UNKNOWN` would not match, and the update would throw.
- The caller gets a domain error, [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md), but the payment is returned as `REFUNDED`. It is not treated as a crash for the DLQ.
